concerns.text: The plan only uses three verified datasets (≈ 10 k rows total) while FR‑008 and SC‑008 require stratified sensitivity analysis across size bins (n < 50, 50‑200, >200) and missingness levels. With only large‑n datasets, the required bins will be empty, making the sensitivity analysis impossible and violating the specification.

No provision is made to acquire additional datasets if a size‑bin or missingness‑level bin lacks a dataset, despite the spec’s explicit requirement that each bin contain ≥ 1 dataset. This undermines the validity of the stratified conclusions.

There is no a priori power analysis to determine whether the available sample size (both number of datasets and per‑dataset row counts) is sufficient to detect meaningful changes in p‑values or effect sizes caused by cleaning. Without power justification, the study may be under‑powered and any observed deltas could be due to random variation.

Permutation FPR is estimated by shuffling the outcome variable (MCAR) while preserving covariates. Real missingness mechanisms (MAR/MNAR) are not simulated, so the FPR estimate may not reflect the true false‑positive behavior under realistic missingness, limiting construct validity of the FPR metric.

Using raw p‑value differences (`p_value_delta`) as the primary indicator of cleaning impact is problematic because p‑values are highly sensitive to sample fluctuations. The plan does not include any variance‑adjusted or confidence‑interval‑based comparison (e.g., overlap of CIs), which would provide a more robust construct for impact assessment.
